main_text.l: bitativis, infinitis. Lucæ 10, τίς τούτων τῶν τριῶν δοκεῖ σοι
πλησίον γεγονέναι; Quis horum trium videtur tibi proximus
Contrá tamen Demosth. ἡδέως ἂν ἐρείμεν τῆς πόλεως μέρος
ἰδὼν ἡ ἐξ ἄλλου τῶν πολιτῶν ἐλέγεῖν ἂν, libenter rogare qualis par-
tis civitatem esse vellet. Sic Plato,
τὰ ποῖα τὰ ζῷα λέγεις; quæ isthæc dicis?
In compositione verò, solet præponi, ut ὁποῖος qualisliber, ὁπόσος quan-
οἷος qualis, ὅσος quantus: τοῖος talis, τόσος tantus.

page.notes: Greek text reproduced from a worn scan; accents and some letters are doubtful. The line ending "tan-" continues on the next page. Some Greek words are approximated where the print is damaged.
